items.title: T3 training-time testing lowers validation loss in data-constrained pretraining
items.summary: Each step takes a trial step on half the batch, tests it on the other half and updates with the meta-gradient. It adds three lines to a first-order step at 6 to 9% extra step time and lowers validation loss by 0.011 to 0.015 nats per token on SlowRun and at 300M, 600M and 1.4B over 8 seeds. Ablations show testing on the same tokens hurts.

doubt.pushback: Authors' own results; no code link was in the posts read.

items.title: InferenceBench adds Fable 5.2, Sonnet 5.5 and Haiku 5.5
items.summary: New InferenceBench results put Fable 5.2 at the same level as Fable 5.1, matching what PostTrainBench showed. The leaderboard post itself is by a collaborator and was quoted, not read in full.

doubt.pushback: Few numbers in the post itself; the leaderboard was not opened.

items.title: Zyphra serves GLM-5.3-Flash on AMD MI300X and lists priced throughput
items.summary: Zyphra says its Optimization Engine puts it on the Artificial Analysis throughput leaderboard for GLM-5.3-Flash on MI300X, at $0.15 input, $0.03 cached and $0.25 output per million tokens, available on Zyphra Inference.

doubt.pushback: Vendor-reported ranking; the leaderboard figure was not opened.

items.title: TensorFold reports 716-729 tok/s combined across four streams for Spark-X2.6-4B on one RTX 5090
items.summary: A thread summarising author tests: four concurrent requests give 716 to 729 tokens/s combined on an RTX 5090 (8-bit, Linux) against 191 to 204 for one stream. At 28k input, decode holds at 197 to 200 tokens/s; a separate RTX 4090 test shows 0.24 s to first token at 2k input and 4.65 s at 29k. The thread notes no drafter or structured-output serving and that the numbers are historical author tests, not a rerun.

doubt.pushback: Thread itself says these are the author's tests, not independently rerun, and the four-stream figure is total throughput rather than per-user speed.

items.title: OpenAI previews automated patching and automated red teaming security tools
items.summary: Codex lead Tibo says OpenAI announced cybersecurity tools it is developing, covering automated patching and automated red teaming, with a recording of the Cyber at the Frontier event. Replies and quotes describe two Daybreak products (Defense Factory and Red Team) and an unnamed cyber model with a reported 77% ExploitGym score; those figures come from third-party posts and the OpenAI page could not be opened.

doubt.pushback: Tools are described as in development; the model score appears only in quote posts and access to the new model is reported as restricted.

reception.summary: The ten non-retweet quotes read were mostly short summaries in English, Chinese and Japanese; some are enthusiastic about auto-patching, others note the strongest model is not available to ordinary users. No one reports trying it.

security_na.reason: OpenAI announcing security tooling, not a vulnerability or compromised component; matches nothing in stack.json.
